art.subject: Velvet Scoter (Melanitta fusca), adult male in winter, as seen from November to March: entire plumage velvety black; a small white crescent below and just behind the eye; white secondaries forming a white patch on the rear of the folded wing, often visible as a white line along the side. Bill mainly yellow-orange on the sides, with black along the base and a small, low black knob where it meets the forehead; iris whitish; legs and feet red.
art.pose: swimming among swells, wing slightly drooped so the white patch shows, side view
art.scene: open winter sea off Korea's east coast with grey swells; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male in winter, side view swimming among swells with the wing slightly drooped: large sea duck with a thick neck, long broad bill and pointed tail, glossy black plumage, pale bluish-grey iris, small white patch below and behind the eye, largely orange-yellow bill, white secondaries showing on the folded wing
adult female, side view swimming: dark brown overall, duller than the male, whitish patches on the side of the face, long broad bill, white secondaries showing on the folded wing

adult male in flight seen squarely from above: head, body and tail in one line, wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, all-black body and wings with a white patch on the secondaries, pointed tail
art.build: Large, heavy sea duck, bigger and bulkier than a Black Scoter, with a long body sitting low in the water. Head fairly large with a sloping forehead running into a long, broad-based bill; feathering projects forward onto the sides of the bill. Bill about as long as the head. Short red legs set far back. In flight the white secondaries show as a clean white rectangle on the rear inner wing, striking against the otherwise all-black wing. Tail short and pointed, often held flat on the water.
avoid: Do not paint a large, hooked black knob with pinkish-red bill sides — that is Stejneger's Scoter (Melanitta stejnegeri), the scoter usually seen in Korea.
Do not leave out the white wing patch; Black Scoter (Melanitta americana) and Surf Scoter have no white in the wing.
Do not add white patches on the forehead or nape (Surf Scoter).
Do not paint the legs black or grey; they are red.
